title: [CPU] inductor::resize_storage_bytes_ leaves tensor metadata larger than its storage

labels.name: module: crash
labels.description: Problem manifests as a hard crash, as opposed to a RuntimeError

labels.name: bot-triaged
labels.description: This is a label only to be used by the auto triage bot

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`inductor::resize_storage_bytes_` can shrink a tensor's backing storage without
updating its existing shape. Later tensor operations trust the unchanged shape
and access beyond the resized storage.

### Reproduction

```python
import torch

t = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.int64)
torch.ops.inductor.resize_storage_bytes_(t, 1)
print(torch.take(t, torch.tensor([7], dtype=torch.int64)))
```

### Error message

An ASAN-enabled CPU build reports an 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow read 55 bytes
after the new one-byte storage. The following is a verbatim excerpt; only
absolute build-root path prefixes were redacted.

```text
==8==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x609000000078 at pc 0x72dd92a7248e bp 0x7fff37c088b0 sp 0x7fff37c088a8
READ of size 8 at 0x609000000078 thread T0
    #0 0x72dd92a7248d in c10::detail::LoadImpl<long>::apply(void const*) <pytorch-source>/c10/util/Load.h:11:12
    #1 0x72dd92a72454 in long c10::load<long>(long const*) <pytorch-source>/c10/util/Load.h:35:10
    #2 0x72dd9f5b240b in at::native::(anonymous namespace)::take_kernel(at::TensorIterator&, at::TensorBase const&)::$_0::operator()() const::'lambda2'()::operator()() const::'lambda'(long&, long const*, long)::operator()(long&, long const*, long) const <pytorch-source>/aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/IndexKernel.cpp:156:3
    #3 0x72dd9f5b223e in void at::native::(anonymous namespace)::cpu_take_put_kernel<long, at::native::(anonymous namespace)::take_kernel(at::TensorIterator&, at::TensorBase const&)::$_0::operator()() const::'lambda2'()::operator()() const::'lambda'(long&, long const*, long)>(at::TensorIterator&, at::TensorBase const&, bool, at::native::(anonymous namespace)::take_kernel(at::TensorIterator&, at::TensorBase const&)::$_0::operator()() const::'lambda2'()::operator()() const::'lambda'(long&, long const*, long) const&, bool)::'lambda'(char**, long const*, long)::operator()(char**, long const*, long) const <pytorch-source>/aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/IndexKernel.cpp:103:7
0x609000000078 is located 55 bytes after 1-byte region [0x609000000040,0x609000000041)
allocated by thread T0 here:
    #0 0x72ddc5e5a617 in __interceptor_posix_memalign <llvm-source>/compiler-rt/lib/asan/asan_malloc_linux.cpp:145:3
    #1 0x72dd8e2a0b61 in c10::alloc_cpu(unsigned long) <pytorch-source>/c10/core/impl/alloc_cpu.cpp:126:13
    #2 0x72dd8e11397a in c10::DefaultCPUAllocator::allocate(unsigned long) <pytorch-source>/c10/core/CPUAllocator.cpp:23:14
    #3 0x72dd92dd2218 in at::native::resize_bytes_cpu(c10::StorageImpl*, unsigned long) <pytorch-source>/aten/src/ATen/native/Resize.cpp:98:38
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow <pytorch-source>/c10/util/Load.h:11:12 in c10::detail::LoadImpl<long>::apply(void const*)
```

### Expected behavior

Shrinking storage should not leave a live tensor whose logical metadata permits
access beyond that storage.

### Additional context

`torch/csrc/inductor/resize_storage_bytes.cpp` directly calls the native
storage-resize routine. It changes the storage byte count but does not update
the live tensor's shape or strides, leaving a reusable metadata/storage
mismatch.
